newsitem.title: USA: MCI launches local phone service in New York area.
newsitem.headline: MCI launches local phone service in New York area.

text.p: MCI Communications Corp. said Friday it will launch local residential telephone service in the New York City area, becoming the first major long distance carrier to break into the nation's largest phone market.

MCI said customers choosing it over NYNEX Corp. will pay 30 cents less per month in telephone line fees than they currently pay the local Baby Bell operator. MCI said it will charge $6.30 per month, while the NYNEX line rate is $6.60.
At the same time, MCI said its plans to offer local service beyond the New York metropolitan area have been hampered by NYNEX.

"... Due to significant operations roadblocks, intentionally constructed by NYNEX, MCI has been forced to limit its initial offering to consumers residing in the New York City metro area, including New York City, Long Island and Westchester County," MCI said in a statement.
"NYNEX isn't playing fair," MCI executive director of brand marketing Judy Levine said. "Their actions demonstrate that they are unable and unwilling to provide efficient and adequate service."
MCI's complaint echoed objections it has raised about other Baby Bell operators around the country as it struggles to enter the $90 billion local phone service market.

MCI accused NYNEX of failing to provide an adequate electronic interface to facilitate the switch of customers to MCI from NYNEX. As a result, MCI claims, it takes three times as long for a customer to order local service from MCI than from NYNEX.
A NYNEX spokesman labeled MCI's assertions "absolutely false and malicious."

"It's extraordinary that MCI is making excuses for itself before it has even opened its first line," NYNEX spokesman Bob Varettoni said. There are 25 other local companies in New York doing just what MCI says they'll have difficulty doing."
